newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi halts Swiss beef imports over BSE fears.
newsitem.headline: Saudi halts Swiss beef imports over BSE fears.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has re-imposed a ban on imports of beef from Switzerland, the country most affected by mad cow disease after Britain, a Saudi newspaper said on Saturday.
The Arabic-language newspaper al-Eqtisadiah did not say when the ban was enforced.
It said it covered "all Swiss cow beef and related products and would stay in place until the European Commission comes out with a stand (on the issue)."
It was not clear if Swiss dairy products and chocolates were included in the ban.
Saudi officials were not immediately available for comment.

The Swiss embassy in Riyadh said Saudi imports of beef and other related goods formed only a fraction of the kingdom's 1995 imports worth 3.4 billion riyal ($1 billion) in mostly Swiss watches and pharmaceuticals.
Saudi Arabia, where meat is a major staple for its 18 million population, removed a ban on similar Swiss products in mid-October.
In addition to local supplies, Saudi Arabia -- the largest market in the region -- imports most of its beef and mutton from New Zealand, Holland, Australia and other European and Arab countries.
Switzerland has reported 230 cases of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), the most of any European country except Britain.
It has announced plans to spend 6.5 million Swiss francs ($4.90 million) to slaughter at least 1,500 cows to eradicate the disease.

The European Union banned exports of British beef last March to protect public health and restore consumer confidence in beef after London raised fears that humans who ate meat of infected animals might become ill with the brain-wasting disease.
